significance.justification: A verified-true result would establish that distinct SAE features causally control belief attribution and factual assertion independently, while their "entanglement ... predicts behavioral conflation" across models—a form-(ii) causal decomposition plus a form-(iii) predictive coupling between feature overlap and behavior. This would establish both a phenomenon (representational overlap covaries with conflation) and a mechanism (separately steerable features produce two different epistemic behaviors), constraining explanations of errors more strongly than the basic SAE feature-and-steering template exemplified by Templeton et al. (2024). A negative result would weaken the clean dictionary-level account, although it would not distinguish distributed representation from SAE failure; true and false states are broadly distinguishable, but "largely disjoint" and "predicts" lack quantitative boundaries. After substituting the topic alone, this score would not remain: the increment comes specifically from the independent causal decomposition and entanglement–error coupling, not from the general importance of LLM beliefs.

reach.justification: The transferable handles are the claimed "entanglement metric" and the intervention of "steering the responsible features"; the former diagnoses conflation and the latter supplies a corrective knob. As stated, the metric is chiefly post hoc because it is correlated with a model's already-measured "behavioral belief/fact conflation rate," rather than forecasting failure before relevant behavior is sampled. After per-model SAE re-extraction, the feature identities must be rediscovered, but the asserted relation—that greater entanglement predicts greater conflation across "model sizes and instruction-tuning stages"—would still predict what researchers should find across a model family; likely downstream users include interpretability researchers and model auditors, though no deployment-time gate is specified. Topic substitution would not preserve this score, because the reach comes from the named cross-checkpoint metric and steering handle rather than merely studying belief representations.
